title: "Resources"
order: 7
---

External links for this lesson. All checked to load from a plain request as of the date this
page was written. (Note: eCFR's own site — ecfr.gov — blocks automated/proxied traffic with a
bot check in this repo's build environment, even though a human browser reaches it fine; the
regulation text quoted in this lesson comes from eCFR's public Versioner API instead, and the
links below use verified-loading mirrors of the same official text.)

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 606.121, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.121)**
  — Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute mirror of the container label requirements
  quoted throughout this lesson, including the full, unabridged text of the machine-readable
  labeling requirement this lesson excerpts. Use this to check the current text and to see the
  product-specific label content (Whole Blood, Red Blood Cells, Plasma, Source Plasma, autologous
  units) this director-level lesson didn't quote in full.

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 610.53, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/610.53)**
  — the dating-period table this lesson draws from to show how one donation's components expire
  on different schedules. Same use case: check for amendments against the dated snapshot in
  `sources/`.

- **[ICCBBA](https://iccbba.org/)** — the nonprofit standards organization that develops and
  administers ISBT 128, the barcode labeling standard this lesson covers in full. Use this as the
  primary source for ISBT 128 itself: what it is, what it covers, and how ICCBBA governs it —
  remember that everything on this site is industry-standard material, not FDA regulation or
  guidance, per this lesson's regulation-versus-standard distinction.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)** — the
  U.S. Government Publishing Office's official, legally authoritative annual CFR archive. Use
  this for the official, dated, legally citable version of a specific year's text — for example,
  to confirm exactly what 606.121 said on the date of a past inspection or a labeling deviation
  investigation.

- **[Overview of the ISBT 128 Standard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rv--jZOBDIs)** (ICCBBA,
  from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. ICCBBA's own explainer of the
  standard it governs, complementing the generic ICCBBA site link above with a direct, narrated
  walkthrough — this is ICCBBA talking about ICCBBA's own standard, about as close to a primary
  source as a video gets for this module. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200; title and channel confirmed verbatim in the response).

- **[BarcodeFAQ: Code 128/GS1-128 Barcode FAQ & Tutorial](https://www.barcodefaq.com/1d/code-128/)**
  — a well-regarded, vendor-neutral technical explainer of the Code 128 barcode symbology ISBT
  128 is built on (the lesson explains where the name comes from; this explains how the symbology
  itself actually encodes characters into bars). Use this if you want the mechanics underneath
  "machine-readable," one layer below what this lesson needs to teach. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: What Is a CMDB? Configuration Management
  Database](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/it-asset-management/cmdb)** — a general ITSM explainer
  on configuration management databases and naming/tagging conventions, the exact concept this
  lesson's ITSM bridge invokes ("ISBT 128 is what a CMDB naming convention would look like if an
  international registration authority enforced it"). Not blood-industry-specific — use it to
  firm up the CMDB-naming-drift analogy, then re-read why a governed product code table is a
  stricter version of the same problem. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[AABB: About AABB Accreditation](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/accreditation)**
  — AABB's own public page on what its accreditation program covers and how the assessment
  process works, for facilities performing blood collection, transfusion services, and related
  activities. Useful for keeping this lesson's four-tier distinction straight: 606.121 is FDA
  *regulation*; AABB accreditation (assessed against AABB Standards, which include labeling and
  product-identification requirements) is a separate, voluntary layer most blood centers also
  hold themselves to. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
